cases.name: Germana "Gemma" Burlakoff
cases.about: Within a few months of her daughter's passing, Linda Villareale turned Gemma's Angels into a nonprofit. Together with granddaughters Bryce (11), Brady (9) and Blain (5), she is active with Aid to Victims of Domestic Abuse (AVDA). Every year, they can be found at AVDA's Run For Hope in their Gemma's Angels T-shirts, raising awareness about the consequences of gun violence.

cases.name: Evelyn Smith Udell
cases.about: She was a retired college librarian. Her obituary said she "earned her Master of Library Science from Drexel University. She worked as a librarian at LaSalle University and Gwynedd Mercy College in Philadelphia before moving to Boca Raton, Florida where she worked in the library at Florida Atlantic University until 2018. Evelyn was a true friend to everyone and loved by all. She loved traveling, her cats, and a good book."
cases.narrative:
He was in her home to install new appliances and beat her with a wooden mallet, then doused her acetone that caught fire and burned almost her entire body. Boca Raton firefighters found her in her the laundry room, bloodied and unconscious. Her head was leaned against a brand new washing machine. Nearby, a new dryer ran its very first test cycle. Both appliances were ordered from Best Buy in the days before. Firefighters said parts of Udell’s body were “smoldering” when they found her and a firefighter got water from a nearby faucet to put out the flames. On top of the washing machine was a wood-handled mallet stained with blood. On the floor were bent prescription glasses and a burnt $1 bill. In the kitchen near the laundry room, the oven and stove burners were turned on. A can of acetone sat on top of the stove, as well as Udell’s open purse and wallet. A thick haze of smoke clouded the home.
